## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Private.Xml. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Signed XML fixes add input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibit DTD processing by default, validate entity references, bound encrypted-data candidate processing, and cap attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/447

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 7.5
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

- **Weakness:** CWE-674 (Uncontrolled Recursion)
## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** All

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

`SignedCms.CheckSignature` can repeatedly reparse attacker-controlled X.509 data, causing unauthenticated quadratic CPU exhaustion.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/468

- **Weakness:** CWE-407 (Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity)

1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Runtime. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

DateTime Hebrew-number parsing can read outside expected stack bounds and terminate the process.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/481

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 7.5
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

- **Weakness:** CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write)
## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** All

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml; System.Private.Xml. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Signed XML fixes add input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibit DTD processing by default, validate entity references, bound encrypted-data candidate processing, and cap attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/490

- **Weakness:** CWE-405 (Asymmetric Resource Consumption (Amplification))

- **Architectures:** All

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

### GHSA-g27p-qf6j-c96c — Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-102870 - ASP.NET Core Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
- Aliases: CVE-2026-102870 | Published: 2026-10-13 | Modified: 2026-11-03 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-94
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected NuGet/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server: introduced:10.0.0 fixed:10.0.14
- Affected NuGet/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server: introduced:11.0.0-preview.1 fixed:11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Blazor WebAssembly debugger included in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server`. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

The Blazor WebAssembly debug proxy evaluates debugger expressions by generating and compiling C# source. Certain values originating in the application being debugged, including `ToString()` results, descriptions, and class names, are embedded in that generated source without consistent escaping. An attacker-controlled value can escape the generated string literal and execute code on a developer's machine when the developer evaluates an expression during debugging.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/445

- **Weakness:** CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection'))

## Affected Platforms

- **Architectures:** All

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml; System.Private.Xml. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Signed XML fixes add input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibit DTD processing by default, validate entity references, bound encrypted-data candidate processing, and cap attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Net.Sockets. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

On Windows, reusing a `SocketAsyncEventArgs` instance across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets can retain an undersized cached native address buffer, allowing an unauthenticated out-of-bounds write during `ReceiveFromAsync`.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/466

- **Weakness:** CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write)

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Localization. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

ASP.NET Core request-localization fallback can add attacker-supplied synthetic culture names to the runtime's global cache, allowing unauthenticated requests to cause unbounded memory growth and denial of service.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/484

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 7.5
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

- **Weakness:** CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling)
## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** All

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Kestrel accepts newline characters in HTTP/2 request trailers and values retrieved from the dynamic HPACK table instead of treating them as malformed.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/462

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Score:** 9.1
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- **Weakness:** CWE-444 (Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling'))

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** All

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

An aborted Kestrel HTTP/1 connection can reparse unread request-body bytes as another request, creating a request-smuggling or desynchronization path.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/472

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Score:** 9.4
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L`
- **Weakness:** CWE-444 (Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling'))

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** All

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime; System.Private.CoreLib. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Unix named-mutex and shared-memory paths can be manipulated through insecure global directories, symlink races, and unsafe permission changes, allowing local attackers to truncate or overwrite files, widen directory permissions, or elevate privileges.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/479

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 7.8
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- **Weakness:** CWE-59 (Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following'))

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** All

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

- Aliases: CVE-2026-96222 | Published: 2026-10-13 | Modified: 2026-10-19 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-295
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected NuGet/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml: introduced:8.0.0 fixed:8.0.5

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

`KeyInfoX509Data` can accept serialized certificate formats containing attacker-controlled chain metadata instead of requiring a plain X.509 certificate, contributing to certificate-forgery and token-spoofing paths.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/474

- **Weakness:** CWE-295 (Improper Certificate Validation)

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** All

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Crafted WPF pixel-shader bytecode can desynchronize the two parsing passes in `CPSTrans::Initialize`, causing heap out-of-bounds writes or reads.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/483

- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 8.8

- **Weakness:** CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write)

- **Architectures:** All

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Restrictive XAML and XPS security fixes block unsafe URI fetching and navigation, propagate untrusted-input state through hyperlink navigation, add TrueType font protection and XAML nesting-depth limits, and avoid caching positive DNS zone-policy decisions.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

WPF XPS hyperlink navigation can bypass URI restrictions and reach an attacker-controlled `ObjectDataProvider`, enabling remote code execution after user interaction.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/456

- **Weakness:** CWE-358 (Improperly Implemented Security Check for Standard)
## Affected Platforms

- **Architectures:** All

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Restrictive XAML and XPS security fixes block unsafe URI fetching and navigation, propagate untrusted-input state through hyperlink navigation, add TrueType font protection and XAML nesting-depth limits, and avoid caching positive DNS zone-policy decisions.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/467

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High

- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

- **Weakness:** CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data)
## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows
- **Architectures:** All

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml; System.Private.Xml. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Signed XML fixes add input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibit DTD processing by default, validate entity references, bound encrypted-data candidate processing, and cap attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/489

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High

- **Weakness:** CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling)
## Affected Platforms

- **Architectures:** All

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Attacker-controlled XPS glyph coordinates can overflow destination pointer arithmetic in `CD3DGlyphBank::RectFillAlpha`, causing an out-of-bounds write and process termination.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/469

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Crafted WPF pixel-shader bytecode can desynchronize the two parsing passes in `CPSTrans::Initialize`, causing heap out-of-bounds writes or reads.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

ASP.NET Core Negotiate LDAP authentication can associate an authenticated identity with an unintended LDAP principal when the LDAP result is not verified against the Kerberos principal SID.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/458

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 7.5
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

- **Weakness:** CWE-290 (Authentication Bypass by Spoofing)
## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS when LDAP claim resolution is enabled
- **Architectures:** All

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime; System.Private.CoreLib. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Unix named-mutex and shared-memory paths can be manipulated through insecure global directories, symlink races, and unsafe permission changes, allowing local attackers to truncate or overwrite files, widen directory permissions, or elevate privileges.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/476

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 7.8
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- **Weakness:** CWE-59 (Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following'))

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** All

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

WPF XPS synthetic hyperlinks exposed through UI Automation can bypass restrictive navigation checks and reach attacker-controlled content, enabling remote code execution after user interaction.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/471

- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 8.8
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

- **Weakness:** CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data)
## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows
- **Architectures:** All

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Crafted WPF pixel-shader bytecode can desynchronize the two parsing passes in `CPSTrans::Initialize`, causing heap out-of-bounds writes or reads.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/450

- **Weakness:** CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write)

- **Architectures:** All

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

An unauthenticated remote attacker can send crafted HTTP/3 reset or abort sequences that deadlock Kestrel connection handling. Repeated requests can cause excessive blocked-thread creation and exhaust server resources, resulting in denial of service.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/461

- **Weakness:** CWE-833 (Deadlock)

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Restrictive XAML and XPS security fixes block unsafe URI fetching and navigation, propagate untrusted-input state through hyperlink navigation, add TrueType font protection and XAML nesting-depth limits, and avoid caching positive DNS zone-policy decisions.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/451

- **Weakness:** CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data)

- **Architectures:** All

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty.

You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue.

### GHSA-7pxr-59rr-hqj2 — Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader vulnerable to denial of service via YAML alias expansion
- Aliases: CVE-2026-72923 | Published: 2026-10-14 | Modified: 2026-10-14 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-400, CWE-770
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- Affected NuGet/Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader: introduced:3.0.0 fixed:3.10.0
- Affected NuGet/Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader: introduced:2.0.0-preview.11 fixed:2.12.0
- Affected NuGet/Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers: introduced:0 fixed:1.6.30

### Impact

A small YAML OpenAPI document containing nested anchors and aliases can cause uncontrolled resource consumption in Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader and Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers. The issue affects OpenAPI document parsing through the public YAML reader APIs and can cause the parsing process to allocate excessive memory and terminate through out-of-memory conditions.

## Affected versions

### Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader

* `>= 2.0.0-preview.11, < 2.12.0`
* `>= 3.0.0, < 3.10.0`

### Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers

* `< 1.6.30`

### Patches

* For the 1.X major version, versions 1.6.30 and above are patched.
* For the 2.X major version, versions 2.12.0 and above are patched.
* For the 3.X major version, versions 3.10.0 and above are patched.

## Impact

Applications, CLIs, developer tools, or services that parse untrusted YAML OpenAPI documents in-process may be terminated by a crafted YAML document containing nested anchors and aliases.

The impact is availability/process termination only. This report does not claim remote code execution, authentication bypass, credential exposure, privilege escalation, data exposure, or Microsoft hosted service impact.

## Details

Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader and Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers parses YAML through SharpYaml. SharpYaml represents aliases as shared `YamlNode` instances in a directed acyclic graph, so the initial parsed YAML graph remains small. During conversion to `System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonNode`, aliases must be materialized as independent nodes because `JsonNode` instances cannot be attached to multiple parents.

Without a bound on that conversion work, a small YAML document using nested anchors and aliases can expand exponentially during conversion. With `N` nested anchors each referenced `k` times, conversion can require `k^N` materialized JSON nodes, leading to excessive memory allocation and possible process termination.

This is an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability, also known as a "billion laughs" style denial of service.

### Example payload

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.0
info:
  title: Test
  version: 0.0.1
paths: {}
x-a: &a ["lol", "lol", "lol", "lol", "lol", "lol", "lol", "lol", "lol"]
x-b: &b [*a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a]
x-c: &c [*b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b]
x-d: &d [*c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c]
x-e: &e [*d, *d, *d, *d, *d, *d, *d, *d, *d]
x-f: &f [*e, *e, *e, *e, *e, *e, *e, *e, *e]
```

## Remediation

Users should upgrade to Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader `2.12.0` or `3.10.0`, or Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers `1.6.30`, depending on the major version line they consume.

The patched versions bound YAML-to-JSON conversion work and fail fast instead of allowing unbounded expansion. The default limits are:

* Maximum materialized node count: `5,000,000`
* Maximum nesting depth: `64`

When the limits are exceeded, `OpenApiYamlReader.Read` reports an `OpenApiDiagnostic` error and does not return a parsed document.

The limits are exposed as process-wide static properties on `YamlConverter` for consumers that need to tune them for trusted workloads:

* `YamlConverter.MaxNodeCount`
* `YamlConverter.MaxDepth`

Applications that parse OpenAPI documents from untrusted sources should avoid parsing those documents in the primary application process when possible. Running parsing in an isolated process can reduce the blast radius of parser failures.

### GHSA-mf2p-h6hf-fcwm — TinyMCE Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability using media plugin `data-mce-object` serialization
- Aliases: CVE-2026-116675 | Published: 2026-10-27 | Modified: 2026-10-27 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-79
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- Affected npm/tinymce: introduced:8.5.1 fixed:8.9.3
- Affected NuGet/TinyMCE: introduced:8.5.1 fixed:8.9.3
- Affected Packagist/tinymce/tinymce: introduced:8.5.1 fixed:8.9.3
- Affected npm/tinymce: introduced:7.9.3 fixed:7.9.4 versions: 7.9.3
- Affected NuGet/TinyMCE: introduced:7.9.3 fixed:7.9.4 versions: 7.9.3
- Affected Packagist/tinymce/tinymce: introduced:7.9.3 fixed:7.9.4 versions: 7.9.3

### Impact
Stored XSS vulnerability in the media plugin. Attackers can inject malicious scripts via elements crafted through the data-mce-object attribute, which are created and executed before sanitization. Impacts users of TinyMCE with the media plugin enabled.

### Patches
This vulnerability has been patched in TinyMCE 8.9.3 and TinyMCE 7.9.4 by ensuring that, when using the media plugin, any content created through the data-mce-object attribute is properly sanitized first.

### Workarounds
No official workaround available.

### Fix
To avoid this vulnerability:

Upgrade to TinyMCE 8.9.3 or higher.
Upgrade to TinyMCE 7.9.4 or higher.

### Acknowledgements
Tiny thanks [Fariskhi Vidyan](https://github.com/farisv) and David Vieira Kurz (HiSolutions AG) for their help identifying this vulnerability.

### GHSA-h26j-4vp7-x9w2 — Metalama: Unsafe deserialization over Metalama's Visual Studio inter-process named pipe enables local code execution
- Aliases: CVE-2026-62848 | Published: 2026-11-03 | Modified: 2026-11-03 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-502, CWE-913
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected NuGet/Metalama.Framework: introduced:2026.1.0-preview fixed:2026.1.19
- Affected NuGet/Metalama.Framework: introduced:0 fixed:2025.1.18
- Affected NuGet/Metalama.Framework: introduced:2026.0.1-preview fixed:2026.0.25

## Summary

Metalama uses a local named-pipe channel to communicate between its Visual Studio processes — the Visual Studio UI process (`devenv`), the out-of-process Roslyn code-analysis process, and the CodeLens process. This channel deserialized messages from the pipe **without restricting which CLR types could be instantiated**. A local process able to write to the pipe can send a crafted message that instantiates arbitrary .NET types — a deserialization primitive in the same class as `BinaryFormatter` (CWE-502), and a well-known gadget-chain code-execution vector.

The flaw is present, via two successive serializers, in **every Metalama release from the first public version (2023.0) up to and including 2026.1.18**, and is fixed in **2026.1.19**.

The pipe name is predictable: `Metalama_{role}_{processId}_{hash(PackageVersion)}`, derived from the public package version and a locally-enumerable process id. This channel is used by the Visual Studio integration only (Windows named pipes); it is not used for command-line / MSBuild builds.

## Mechanisms

**JSON era — Metalama 2023.0 through 2026.0.x (Newtonsoft.Json).** The pipe formatter enabled polymorphic type embedding:
```csharp
formatter.JsonSerializer.TypeNameHandling = TypeNameHandling.All;   // ServiceEndpoint.cs (early), later BaseEndpoint.cs
```
The accompanying `SerializationBinder` (added later for multi-version assembly support) only **remapped assembly names**; its `BindToType` resolved **any** type name from the wire (`assembly.GetType(typeName)`) with **no type allow-list**. `TypeNameHandling.All` is the canonical unsafe-deserialization setting and has publicly available gadget chains (e.g. ysoserial.net), so this era is at least as exploitable as the later one. (Introduced by commit `0554368737`, first shipped in `release/2023.0.101-rc`.)

**MessagePack era — Metalama 2026.1.0 through 2026.1.18.** The 2026.1 line migrated the pipe serialization to MessagePack (PR #1299, commit `117b607805`, 2026-01-29), using **typeless** MessagePack (`TypelessObjectResolver`), which likewise embeds CLR type names on the wire and instantiates arbitrary types on receipt — again with no allow-list.

Both mechanisms share the same channel, the same predictable pipe name, the same impact, and the same access preconditions.

## Impact

Potential arbitrary code execution inside the Visual Studio process that hosts the affected component (the UI process, the code-analysis process, or the CodeLens process), with full loss of confidentiality, integrity and availability within that process.

**Mitigating factor (limits practical severity to Medium):** the pipe is created with the default Windows ACL (no explicit `PipeSecurity`), which permits **only same-user processes to write**. All of the Visual Studio processes involved run as the same logged-in developer, so exploitation requires the attacker to already be executing code as that same user. There is **no privilege escalation** and no crossing of a security boundary; the practical value is code execution inside the developer's Visual Studio session (lateral movement / persistence within an already same-user-compromised context). This is why the practical severity is **Medium** despite the CVSS base score.

## Severity

CVSS v3.1: `AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` = **7.3 (High)** base score; **practical severity Medium**, because the attacker gains no privilege beyond what they already had (same user, same Visual Studio session).

CVSS v4.0 cross-check: `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` = 7.0 (High). The Subsequent-System metrics are None because no security boundary is crossed.

## Affected products and remediation

All affected products are part of the Visual Studio integration.

| Product | Affected | Remediation |
|---|---|---|
| NuGet `Metalama.Framework` | all `< 2026.1.19` | upgrade to **2026.1.19** (no backports) |
| VS extension `PostSharpTechnologies.PostSharp` ("Metalama + PostSharp", maintained) | **2024.1 - 2026.1.4** | update to **2026.1.5** (bundles Metalama 2026.1.19) |
| VS extension `PostSharpTechnologies.Metalama` (retired) | all versions | uninstall / migrate to PostSharp `>= 2026.1.5` |
| VS extension `PostSharpTechnologies.caravela` (retired) | all versions | uninstall / migrate to PostSharp `>= 2026.1.5` |

The PostSharp extension was a separate, Metalama-free product before the 2024.1 merge (Metalama.Vsx issue #33843), so earlier PostSharp versions are not affected. GitHub has no Visual Studio Marketplace ecosystem, so only the NuGet package appears in the structured "Affected products" list.

## Fix

Fixed in Metalama **2026.1.19** (commit `d97f52e1b5`, PR #1651): the type-name deserialization is wrapped in `RpcContractMessagePackOptions`, which enforces a `[RpcContract]` type allow-list on the wire; pipe access is restricted to the current user. The fix reaches the maintained Visual Studio extension in version **2026.1.5**. The retired Caravela and Metalama extensions will not be fixed.

## Executive summary

A buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the Brotli decompression library used by .NET. This vulnerability may allow an unauthenticated attacker to read or corrupt process memory. This could lead to information disclosure, denial of service, or elevation of privilege.

ASP.NET Core and HttpClient do not automatically decompress Brotli data in their default configurations. Applications are exposed when they enable Brotli decompression or explicitly use Brotli decompression APIs to process attacker-controlled data, as described below. .NET Framework is not affected.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/494

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 8.1
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C`
- **Weakness:** CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write)

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** All
- **Architectures:** All

## Mitigations

ASP.NET Core request decompression and HttpClient automatic response decompression are not enabled by default. An application is not exposed merely because an affected .NET package is installed. Exposure requires the application to decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data through one of these paths:

- Enable ASP.NET Core [automatic request decompression](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/middleware/request-decompression) with Brotli (`br`) support.
- Enable HttpClient automatic response decompression by configuring [HttpClientHandler.AutomaticDecompression](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.net.http.httpclienthandler.automaticdecompression) or [SocketsHttpHandler.AutomaticDecompression](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.net.http.socketshttphandler.automaticdecompression) to include [DecompressionMethods.Brotli](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.net.decompressionmethods) or `DecompressionMethods.All`.
- Explicitly use Brotli decompression APIs in `System.IO.Compression`, such as `BrotliStream` or `BrotliDecoder`.

Until the update can be deployed, avoid decompressing attacker-controlled Brotli data.

The following examples show how to disable Brotli decompression if you are already using it.

> **Warning: Do not use these code snippets if you are not already using decompression.** Do not introduce a call to `AddRequestDecompression` if your application does not already call it. Similarly, do not introduce an `AutomaticDecompression` property assignment if your application does not already set that property. Modify only your existing decompression configuration. Enabling automatic decompression can introduce denial-of-service risks even when Brotli is excluded.

If you are already using Brotli request decompression in ASP.NET Core, exclude it by removing the `br` entry from your existing decompression configuration. This retains the default gzip and deflate providers:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddRequestDecompression(options =>
{
    options.DecompressionProviders.Remove("br");
});
```

If your application already enables HttpClient automatic response decompression, disable Brotli by updating the flags on your existing handler so they do not include `DecompressionMethods.Brotli`:

```csharp
var handler = new HttpClientHandler
{
    AutomaticDecompression = DecompressionMethods.GZip | DecompressionMethods.Deflate
};

var httpClient = new HttpClient(handler);
```

Applications that directly use Brotli decompression APIs must stop passing untrusted Brotli data to those APIs until updated. Ensure that other application code does not continue to decompress the same untrusted Brotli data. These changes can affect normal request and response handling and should be tested before deployment. Installing the security update remains the recommended fix.

## <a name="affected-packages"></a>Affected Packages

The vulnerability affects .NET applications using an affected Brotli decoder in the runtime or NativeAOT packages listed below.

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

You are affected if your application uses an affected Brotli decoder included in a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), including a decoder linked into a NativeAOT application, to decompress attacker-controlled data. See [mitigations](#mitigations) for the affected usage paths and default settings.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

Install the updated runtime or SDK for the .NET version used by your application. If your application directly references an affected package, update that reference to the patched version listed above.

.NET release | Runtime | SDK versions
------------ | ------- | ------------
.NET 8 | 8.0.33 | 8.0.133, 8.0.427
.NET 9 | 9.0.22 | 9.0.123, 9.0.320
.NET 10 | 10.0.14 | 10.0.114, 10.0.403
.NET 11 previews | 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148

Download .NET from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

If you have deployed [self-contained applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments), rebuild and redeploy those applications with the updated runtime.

For NativeAOT applications, update the SDK and any explicit compiler or runtime-pack references to patched versions, then republish and redeploy the application. Updating the machine's shared runtime alone does not replace a decoder already linked into a NativeAOT executable.

## Other Information

### Reporting Security Issues

If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue).

Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty.

### Support

You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components.

Multipart form processing can bypass the configured header-count limit and consume excessive resources.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/511

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 7.5 (base score)
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C`
- **Weakness:** CWE-770

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** All

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

Check the deployed runtime and application package versions against the affected ranges above. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

Install the applicable runtime or update each independently referenced package to the fixed version above. After updating standalone packages, rebuild and redeploy affected applications, including framework-dependent applications; restarting alone does not replace app-local packages. Restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy self-contained applications; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace their embedded runtime. An SDK update alone does not update an application's standalone package references.

### GHSA-f7vh-h5g3-7jrh — Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120006 - Aspire Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
- Aliases: CVE-2026-120006 | Published: 2026-11-10 | Modified: 2026-11-10 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-201
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected NuGet/Aspire.Hosting.AppHost: introduced:0 fixed:13.6.5
- Affected NuGet/Aspire.Hosting: introduced:0 fixed:13.6.5

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components.

Disclosure of an Aspire Dashboard authentication cookie to a linked service can allow an attacker-controlled container to replay the authenticated session and execute code as the host developer.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/503

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 7.5
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- **Weakness:** CWE-201 (Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data)

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** macOS
- **Architectures:** x64, Arm64

## <a name="affected-packages"></a>Affected Packages

### Standalone Aspire

Package | Affected version | Patched version
--- | --- | ---
[Aspire.Hosting.AppHost](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting.AppHost) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5
[Aspire.Hosting](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5

The affected scenario involves a Dashboard-authenticated AppHost workflow with an attacker-controlled container and a linked HTTPS YARP gateway. The affected hosting code is in `Aspire.Hosting`, a dependency of `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost`. `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` supplies the AppHost package implicitly unless the project overrides the default references.

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

The reported scenario involves a developer starting an Aspire AppHost, authenticating to its Dashboard, and following a resource link that routes to an attacker-controlled container. All released versions through 13.6.4 are affected.

Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire components have been updated.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

Update the AppHost project's `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost` package reference to version 13.6.5 or later. If the project obtains this package implicitly through `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk`, update that SDK reference to version 13.6.5 or later. Explicit package references or central version pins must also resolve `Aspire.Hosting` to version 13.6.5 or later. Restore dependencies, rebuild, and restart the AppHost after updating.

Updating only the .NET runtime, .NET SDK, Aspire CLI, or standalone Dashboard does not replace the AppHost project's hosting dependencies.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components.

SignalR connections are not consistently bound to the identity negotiated at connection establishment, allowing injected messages to execute Hub invocations as the victim.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/504

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Score:** 9.0 (base score)
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C`
- **Weakness:** CWE-863

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** All

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

Check the deployed runtime and application package versions against the affected ranges above. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

Install the applicable runtime or update each independently referenced package to the fixed version above. After updating standalone packages, rebuild and redeploy affected applications, including framework-dependent applications; restarting alone does not replace app-local packages. Restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy self-contained applications; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace their embedded runtime. An SDK update alone does not update an application's standalone package references.

### Reporting Security Issues

If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue).

Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty.

### Support

You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components.

SignalR Redis scale-out can mishandle case-mismatched group removal and leave subscriptions in a state that permits persistent resource amplification and denial of service.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/509

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 7.5 (base score)
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C`
- **Weakness:** CWE-401

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** All

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

Compare the deployed ASP.NET Core runtime and the application's resolved Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.StackExchangeRedis package version with the affected ranges above. Self-contained applications include their own runtime.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

Update both the ASP.NET Core runtime and the Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.StackExchangeRedis package to the applicable patched versions above. Restart affected framework-dependent applications after installing the runtime update. Rebuild and redeploy applications after updating the package; self-contained applications must also be rebuilt with the patched runtime. Updating a machine-wide runtime or SDK alone does not update an application's standalone package references.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components.

An insecure temporary directory used by Aspire CLI-generated builds can allow a local attacker to influence MSBuild response-file discovery and execute code with the privileges of the developer running the CLI.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/519

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 7.3
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- **Weakness:** CWE-379 (Creation of Temporary File in Directory with Insecure Permissions)
- **MSRC severity:** Important

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Linux, macOS
- **Architectures:** x64, Arm64

The affected scenario concerns CLI-generated server and integration builds on non-Windows systems when a local attacker can influence automatic MSBuild response-file discovery through an attacker-writable directory. This includes builds started by `aspire sdk generate`, `aspire sdk dump`, and `aspire sdk export`.

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

The reported scenario involves a local attacker influencing a generated build through a shared temporary-directory ancestor while another user invokes the Aspire CLI. Versions 13.2.0 through 13.6.4 are affected.

Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

Update the Aspire CLI to version 13.6.5 or later. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method.

Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated.

If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components.

An oversized Portable PDB document name can be truncated during allocation and cause a heap out-of-bounds write.

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 8.8 (base score)
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C`
- **Weakness:** CWE-122

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows
- **Architectures:** x86, x64, Arm64

## <a name="affected-packages"></a>Affected Packages

Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native components bundled with the affected .NET versions listed below are affected when initializing the native reader with a Portable PDB containing an oversized document name. The Windows runtime's native stack-trace reader can reach this initialization through its native-reader fallback.

### .NET on Windows

Product | Affected version | Patched version
--- | --- | ---
.NET 8.0 installed on Windows | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.34 | 8.0.34
.NET 9.0 installed on Windows | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.23 | 9.0.23
.NET 10.0 installed on Windows | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.15 | 10.0.15
.NET 11.0 installed on Windows | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0

### Windows runtime packages for self-contained applications

The following packages deliver the affected .NET native reader. Exposure requires the PDB-reading operation described above; the presence of the reader does not make every application or symbol-reading path vulnerable.

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

Applications using Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native components bundled with the affected .NET versions listed above to initialize the native reader with a Portable PDB containing an oversized document name are exposed on Windows x86, x64, and Arm64. The Windows runtime's native stack-trace reader can reach this initialization when PE metadata selects its native-reader fallback. See [affected packages](#affected-packages) for the affected .NET products on Windows.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

Update affected .NET installations and each installed SDK feature band to the versions listed above or later. If an SDK was installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio as well.

For applications that deploy their own .NET runtime, including self-contained applications, update the runtime used to build the application, rebuild, and redeploy. Updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace an application's embedded runtime. Restart processes that have loaded the affected native reader.

## <a name="affected-packages"></a>Affected Packages

Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native components bundled with the affected .NET versions listed below are affected when initializing the native reader with a crafted Portable PDB containing an `EmbeddedSource` record with parent RID 0. The Windows runtime's native stack-trace reader can reach this initialization through its native-reader fallback.

### .NET on Windows

Product | Affected version | Patched version
--- | --- | ---
.NET 8.0 installed on Windows | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.34 | 8.0.34
.NET 9.0 installed on Windows | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.23 | 9.0.23
.NET 10.0 installed on Windows | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.15 | 10.0.15
.NET 11.0 installed on Windows | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0

### Windows runtime packages for self-contained applications

The following packages deliver the affected .NET native reader. Exposure requires the PDB-reading operation described above; the presence of the reader does not make every application or symbol-reading path vulnerable.

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

Applications using Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native components bundled with the affected .NET versions listed above to initialize the native reader with a crafted Portable PDB containing an `EmbeddedSource` record with parent RID 0 are exposed on x86, x64, and Arm64. The Windows runtime's native stack-trace reader can reach this initialization when PE metadata selects its native-reader fallback. See [affected packages](#affected-packages) for the affected .NET products on Windows.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

Update affected .NET installations and each installed SDK feature band to the versions listed above or later. If an SDK was installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio as well.

For applications that deploy their own .NET runtime, including self-contained applications, update the runtime used to build the application, rebuild, and redeploy. Updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace an application's embedded runtime. Restart processes that have loaded the affected native reader.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components.

A crafted PDB `LF_DECIMAL` payload can trigger an out-of-bounds stack write when processed by DIA.

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 8.8 (base score)
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C`
- **Weakness:** CWE-502, CWE-121

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows
- **Architectures:** x86, x64, Arm64

## <a name="affected-packages"></a>Affected Packages

Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native versions earlier than 18.9.1-beta1.26515.1 are affected when reading constants from attacker-supplied PDBs through `ISymUnmanagedConstant.GetValue`. The .NET runtime's native stack-trace reading path does not call `ISymUnmanagedConstant.GetValue`. This excludes that invocation, not the .NET product as a whole.

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

Applications using Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native versions earlier than 18.9.1-beta1.26515.1 to read constants from attacker-supplied PDBs through `ISymUnmanagedConstant.GetValue` are exposed on x86, x64, and Arm64. The .NET runtime's native stack-trace reading path does not call `ISymUnmanagedConstant.GetValue`. This excludes that invocation, not the .NET product as a whole. See [affected packages](#affected-packages) for the affected .NET products on Windows.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

Update affected .NET installations and each installed SDK feature band to the versions listed above or later. If an SDK was installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio as well.

Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native is delivered through .NET Core rather than as a standalone customer NuGet update. For applications that deploy their own affected .NET runtime, including self-contained applications, update the runtime used to build the application, rebuild, and redeploy. Updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace an application's embedded runtime. Restart processes that have loaded the affected native reader.

## Advisory FAQ

### <a name="how-affected"></a>How do I know if I am affected?

Applications using Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native versions earlier than 18.9.1-beta1.26515.1 to load document specifications from a PDB that references an attacker-influenced COFF object are exposed on x86, x64, and Arm64. The SDK distributions listed above are affected through their bundled .NET runtime. See [affected packages](#affected-packages) for the affected .NET products on Windows.

### <a name="how-fix"></a>How do I fix the issue?

Update affected .NET installations and each installed SDK feature band to the versions listed above or later. If an SDK was installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio as well.

Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native is delivered through .NET Core rather than as a standalone customer NuGet update. For applications that deploy their own affected .NET runtime, including self-contained applications, update the runtime used to build the application, rebuild, and redeploy. Updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace an application's embedded runtime. Restart processes that have loaded the affected native reader.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components.

Crafted PDB line metadata can exceed the caller-provided buffer and cause a heap out-of-bounds write.

## CVSS Details

- **Version:** 3.1
- **Severity:** High
- **Score:** 8.8 (base score)
- **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C`
- **Weakness:** CWE-122

## Affected Platforms

- **Platforms:** Windows
- **Architectures:** x86, x64, Arm64
